label: monk2-s5
summary: This MONK-2 network has one hidden unit and ten direct edges, and it computes a count band. The direct score falls with each attribute at its first value; the hidden ReLU unit (node 217) fires on the 89 training rows with at most one first value (share 100%) and cancels their high direct score, and on 0 of the 143 rows with three or more. What remains positive is the band of exactly two first values, the target concept: of the 432 input combinations the model says yes on 0 outside that band and agrees with the exactly-two rule on 384. Most of its misses are positives that pair a6=1 with a first value of a1, a2, a4 or a5, because a6=1 lowers the direct score the most; the rule "exactly two, and not a6=1 without a3=1" agrees on 428 of 432. On the training split the model ranks the rows perfectly (AUC 1.000) but its accuracy at a risk cut of one half is 89.0%, largely because the 35 positive rows of that a6=1 pattern get a mean predicted risk of 0.14. Switching the gate off lowers the training AUC to 0.616; holding the direct score at its mean lowers it to 0.675.

(3) Three add_evidence calls returned lint warnings that were not captured; one suspected narrative (enumeration scope) was amended, and the final recheck reports no open issues.
